text: Then Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, across from Jericho. And the LORD showed him the whole land: Gilead as far as Dan,
all of Naphtali, the territory of Ephraim and Manasseh, all the land of Judah as far as the Western Sea,
the Negev, and the whole plain—the valley of Jericho, the City of Palms—as far as Zoar.

versions.text: the Negev, and the whole region from the valley of Jericho, the City of Palms, as far as Zoar.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew places הַכִּכָּר (the plain/basin) in apposition to "the valley of Jericho," not as a region measured "from" it. The word "from" adds a spatial idea not in the text; an appositional rendering is more accurate and still reads smoothly aloud.

text: Then the LORD said to him, "This is the land I swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob when I said, 'I will give it to your descendants.' I have let you see it with your own eyes, but you will not cross over into it."
So Moses, the servant of the LORD, died there in the land of Moab, as the LORD had said.

He buried him in the valley in the land of Moab, opposite Beth Peor, but to this day no one knows where his grave is.<note>The Hebrew verb is singular with an unstated subject; the implied subject is understood to be the LORD, though it may also be read impersonally, "he was buried."</note>

versions.text: He buried him in the valley in the land of Moab, opposite Beth Peor, but to this day no one knows where his grave is.
versions.explanation: The subject of "He buried him" is unexpressed in Hebrew and ambiguous to a listener; a brief footnote clarifies without altering the reading text.

text: Moses was a hundred and twenty years old when he died, yet his eyes were not weak nor his strength gone.
The Israelites mourned for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days, until the time of weeping and mourning for Moses was over.
Now Joshua son of Nun was filled with the spirit of wisdom, because Moses had laid his hands on him. So the Israelites listened to him and did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Never again has a prophet risen in Israel like Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face,
who performed all those signs and wonders the LORD sent him to do in the land of Egypt—to Pharaoh, to all his servants, and to his whole land—
and who displayed all that mighty power and all those great and terrifying deeds that Moses did in the sight of all Israel.
